answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove misbehavior, like tending a garden where only planted identities grow trust over time. Newcomers start with limited permissions and must forge a record of honest, verifiable work across many rounds before gaining full access, so creating thousands of fake agents at dawn of a new market costs real capital and time per identity. An attacker who splits stake across clones weakens each one, while honest agents compound reputation, making mass forgery unprofitable.
